title: Column type propagated to the right sice of a boolean expression inconsistently
body:
### Describe the bug

When using bind parameters with boolean expression the type of the column is inconsistently propagated to the bind parameter

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

1.4, 2

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

any

### Database Vendor and Major Version

any

### Python Version

any

### Operating system

any

### To Reproduce

```python
import sqlalchemy as sa

tbl = sa.table("foo", sa.column("d", sa.Date), sa.column("i", sa.Integer))

for case in (
    tbl.c.d == "2023-01-01",
    tbl.c.i == "123",
    tbl.c.d.in_(["2023-01-01"]),
    tbl.c.i.in_(["123"]),
    sa.tuple_(tbl.c.d, tbl.c.i) == ("2023-01-01", "123"),
    sa.tuple_(tbl.c.d, tbl.c.i).in_([("2023-01-01", "123")]),
):
    print(case, case.right.type)
```


### Error

The previous code prints
in 2
```
foo.d = :d_1 VARCHAR
foo.i = :i_1 VARCHAR
foo.d IN (__[POSTCOMPILE_d_1]) VARCHAR
foo.i IN (__[POSTCOMPILE_i_1]) VARCHAR
(foo.d, foo.i) = (:param_1, :param_2) TupleType(String(), String())
(foo.d, foo.i) IN (__[POSTCOMPILE_param_1]) TupleType(Date(), Integer())
```
in 1.4
```
foo.d = :d_1 VARCHAR
foo.i = :i_1 VARCHAR
foo.d IN (__[POSTCOMPILE_d_1]) VARCHAR
foo.i IN (__[POSTCOMPILE_i_1]) VARCHAR
(foo.d, foo.i) = (:param_1, :param_2) TupleType(Unicode(), Unicode())
(foo.d, foo.i) IN (__[POSTCOMPILE_param_1]) TupleType(Date(), Integer())
```

While the types are slightly different in 1.4 and v2 the behaviour is the same.

In particular only when using tuple_() with an in_ statement are the types properly propagated to the right sice, in all other cases the types of the bingparams seems interfered from the value.

I would expect that the bindparam types are either always derived from the value or always derived from the left side

I've not tested all combination so there may be other behaviours too.

### Additional context

I've discovered this behaviours since when updating to v2 I wanted to remove a custom literal dialect that supported literal compile of date types.
Since psycopg2 allows passing dates as strings I've found that the when using equality the internal dialect could literal compile such statement (like  `tbl.c.d == "2023-01-01"` above), but when using it inside a tuple it could not (like `sa.tuple_(tbl.c.d, tbl.c.i).in_([("2023-01-01", "123")])` above), since the fist uses the literal processor for String while the second the one for Date that only accepts date instances
